title: Moroccan-Spiced Chicken with Grilled Peach Couscous & Lemon Yogurt
summary: A light late-summer dinner of warmly spiced chicken, pearl couscous tossed with charred peaches and vegetables, salty feta, and a cool lemon-garlic yogurt sauce.
sourceNote: Developed with ChatGPT as a light, summery dinner using an easy pantry approximation of ras el hanout rather than requiring a specialty spice blend.

steps.text: Make the spice blend by combining the cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, allspice, optional clove or nutmeg, and optional cayenne. Measure about 1 1/2 tablespoons of the blend for the chicken; reserve any extra for another use.

Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon olive oil, the measured spice blend, 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt, 1 teaspoon honey, and the zest of half the lemon. Let it stand while the remaining ingredients are prepared.
Cook the pearl couscous according to the package directions. Drain if necessary, then spread it in a wide bowl so it can cool slightly while the chicken and vegetables cook.

Preheat a Blackstone or large heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Lightly oil the cooking surface if needed. Add the zucchini and bell pepper and cook until browned at the edges but still slightly crisp, about 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.

Place the peach wedges cut-side down on the hot griddle. Cook without moving for 60 to 90 seconds per cut side, just until caramelized and lightly charred. Remove and cut larger wedges into bite-sized pieces if desired.

Add the seasoned chicken to the hot griddle in one uncrowded layer. Leave it undisturbed for about 2 minutes to develop a dark aromatic crust, then turn and continue cooking until browned and the thickest pieces reach 165°F, about 5 to 7 minutes total depending on size.
Remove the chicken from the heat and immediately squeeze about 1 tablespoon lemon juice over it. Rest for 3 to 5 minutes while finishing the couscous.

Toss the warm couscous with the charred zucchini and pepper, cucumber, red onion, chickpeas if using, grilled peaches, feta, 1 teaspoon olive oil, about 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and the mint if using. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. The salad should be warm or room temperature rather than piping hot.

Make the lemon-garlic yogurt by stirring together the Greek yogurt, grated garlic, about 1 tablespoon lemon juice, a little remaining lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and black pepper. Thin with 1 to 2 tablespoons water until it is easily spoonable.

Spoon the grilled peach couscous onto plates, top with the Moroccan-spiced chicken, and finish generously with the cool lemon yogurt. Serve extra spice blend or hot sauce at the table for anyone who wants more heat.
